messages:

To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jul 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal questions: pricing + SLA asks

Marcus —

Quick and direct: after the recent incidents and the pricing pressure from our board, Aurora is not in a position to accept the current renewal terms. Before we make a decision we need a written offer that includes the following: 

- a material price reduction (target ~25% off list for year 1),
- an operational credit for the two major incidents in Q2 (we're thinking ~$60k),
- a 12-month term reset (we need the team to start from a fresh 12 month commitment),
- a firm SLA of 99.95% with financial remedies for breaches.

This is time sensitive — our procurement committee meets Thursday and we need a formal concession proposal to present. Happy to do a quick call this afternoon if that helps.

Thanks,
Elaine Park

Team — forwarding Elaine's note. Aurora is at imminent risk. Summary of asks: ~25% discount, ~$60k credit, 12mo term reset, SLA 99.95% w/ financials.

My recommended concession package (to keep this within acceptable impact):
- One-time credit: $40,000 (operational credit for Q2 incidents)
- One-year term reset on a 12-month renewal with 20% off year-1 list pricing
- SLA uplift to 99.9% for the next 12 months with capped financial credits (up to 50% of monthly bill per incident, limited total exposure)

Rationale: keeps retention economics reasonable, buys time to complete reliability fixes and provides Aurora visible SLA commitments. Attached is a quick model showing net dollar impact vs. lifetime value. Need approval or steer before I respond to Elaine; procurement meets Thu.

Attachments: aurora_concession_model.xlsx

—Marcus

Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal questions: pricing + SLA asks — urgent approval request

Marissa / Jasmine — attached is the quick financial model (see tab 'Offer vs Churn') that runs three scenarios: conservative (10% discount + credit), recommended (20% + $40k credit), and aggressive (25% + $60k credit). Key points: 

- With Aurora's ARR (~$480k), our model shows the recommended package (20% + $40k credit + 12mo reset) results in a net present value that is positive compared to losing the account (even allowing for a 15% uplift in support hours).
- The aggressive package achieves a slightly higher retention probability but reduces YoY margin materially.
- SLA uplift to 99.9% with targeted compensations limits our maximum exposure to ~2 months of billings at most in the modeled worst-case.

I'm including proposed amendment bullet points to share with Legal: 
- Term: new effective renewal date + 12 months guaranteed term starting on execution date.
- Pricing: 20% off year-1 list; baseline ratchet back to standard thereafter.
- Credits: one-time $40,000 operational credit applied to first invoice.
- SLA: commitment to 99.9% platform availability; breach credits up to 50% of monthly invoice for an incident; total annual exposure capped at 100% of monthly invoice.

Attachments: aurora_concession_model.xlsx, aurora_offer_v1.pdf

If we get Karthik's ok, I'll share the offer with Elaine and request expedited legal redline.

—Marcus

Marcus / team — reviewed the model. Approve the recommended package with the following constraints: 

1) Approve: 20% off year-1 list, one-time $40k operational credit, 12-month term reset.
2) SLA: approve 99.9% commitment with financial credit language as proposed, but cap total annual exposure to one monthly invoice (we cannot exceed that).
3) Condition: require Aurora commit to a customer success-led remediation plan (CSM QBR + technical deep-dive) within 30 days of execution; failure to engage voids concession.
4) Finance: Marcus please assign the finance write-off code and ensure legal routes amendment for signature.

Once Marcus confirms you have the finance code and Legal prepping the amendment, approve sending to customer. Karthik
